body: In February 2019, Hembree Insurance Trust leased a 135,847-square-foot industrial building in Scottsboro, Alabama to Maples Industries, Inc. for five years, from January 1, 2020 through December 31, 2024. Maples, already in possession under a lease dating to 2011, was responsible for maintenance and for roof replacement or repair, with Hembree paying 50% of agreed roof replacement or major repair costs. Hembree sued on March 3, 2024, alleging Maples had failed to repair or replace the roof.

Maples moved to dismiss, arguing Hembree did not own the property because a 2014 warranty deed showed it had transferred the building to Woods Cove Industrial Property, LLC. Hembree responded that it was Woods Cove's sole member, with authority under the LLC's operating agreement to manage it and act as its agent. On July 17, 2024, the Jackson Circuit Court treated the motion as one for summary judgment and declared the lease "null and void in all respects."

The Alabama Supreme Court reversed on April 11, 2025, in an opinion by Chief Justice Stewart, Insurance Business reported. The Court held that a lessor need not own property to lease it if it lawfully possesses or controls it, and that under long-standing Alabama law a tenant in possession generally cannot dispute its landlord's title. Because Hembree placed Maples in possession, Maples paid rent and had the benefit of possession, Maples was estopped from challenging the lease on that basis. The Court did not decide whether fraud, misrepresentation or mistake claims could arise from the ownership issue.

After remand, Hembree appealed again from the Jackson Circuit Court in the same case. On October 31, 2025, the Supreme Court affirmed without opinion; the order does not describe the judgment under review.

timeline.label: Hembree Insurance Trust and Maples Industries sign a five-year industrial lease in Scottsboro
Hembree sues Maples for failing to repair the roof as required by the lease
Jackson Circuit Court declares the lease void because title had passed to Woods Cove
Alabama Supreme Court reverses, holding Maples generally cannot dispute its landlord's title, and remands
On Hembree's second appeal, the Alabama Supreme Court affirms without opinion
